name: Michael Bennet
stance: Wants a new Federal Digital Commission that pre-certifies frontier models and can pause release of models posing catastrophic risk for up to six months.

statements.text: President Trump's reckless and short-sighted decision to let NVIDIA sell advanced AI chips to China threatens U.S. national security and technological leadership.
Offered an amendment, blocked by Republicans, to add ethics guardrails after the administration approved sales of advanced AI chips to the UAE despite national security concerns.
Secured Senate Intelligence Committee passage of his amendment requiring national security assessments before exports of advanced AI technology.
The CEOs of the major artificial intelligence companies themselves are sounding the alarm on unchecked AI. Yet President Trump continues to look the other way.

Released the AI Regulator Act proposal with Sen. Welch, giving a Federal Digital Commission pre-clearance of frontier models, six-month pauses on catastrophic-risk releases, and fines up to 15% of global revenue.
The challenge posed by a new technology and a new industry able to profoundly transform our economy and society is one we have faced before.
AI companies need to face real consequences, including the power to pause unsafe technology and impose serious penalties of up to 15% of global revenue.

Responding to a report that AI safety rules were dropped after a donation from OpenAI's president to a pro-Trump super PAC, called for an independent agency with authority to set and enforce AI rules.
Announced he is introducing legislation to create an independent agency to oversee AI and ensure AI companies follow the rules.
This is exactly why we need an impartial regulator to assess powerful new AI models for serious risks before they reach the public.
We cannot rely on President Trump's honor system to protect the American people from the serious risks of AI.
AI is too powerful to regulate through a handshake agreement.
